info.name: THE FOOLS JOURNEY - Magic Items
info.description: Homebrew magic items for THE FOOLS JOURNEY campaign.

description.p: This shield grants the bearer the ability to use the Menacing Attack maneuver once per short or long rest without expending a superiority die. It also grants a +1 bonus to AC. This shield’s design resonates with Agamar’s heritage and prowess in battle.

Menacing Attack. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to attempt to frighten the target. You add the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll, and the target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it is frightened of you until the end of your next turn. The DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (whichever is higher).

setters.set: shield, orc, maneuver, menacing attack, frightened

description.p: A gauntlet made of dark, crystalline scales, pulsing with internal energy. When worn, the user’s arm glows faintly with blue or purple lightning-like cracks. Runes in the shape of tentacles swirl across the surface, hinting at its abyssal origins.
Abyssal Descent. The gauntlet can unleash a powerful area-of-effect attack, mimicking the descent of a kraken into battle.

ul.li: Activation: As an action, you leap up to 30 feet into the air and slam down onto a point you choose within 60 feet, causing a violent shockwave upon impact.

Effect: All creatures within a 15-foot radius must succeed on a DC 18 Strength saving throw or take 6d10 force damage, be knocked prone, and suffer vulnerability to the next instance of bludgeoning, force, or thunder damage within the next round. On a success, targets take half damage and remain standing.
Feature: If a creature’s hit points drop below 20% due to this effect, they are instantly incapacitated and trapped by shadowy tendrils until the end of your next turn.
Recharge: This ability recharges after a long rest or when you score a critical hit with a melee weapon while attuned to the gauntlet.

description.p: Ceaseless Surge. After activating Abyssal Descent, the gauntlet grants you a surge of abyssal power.

ul.li: You gain temporary hit points equal to half the damage dealt by the shockwave.
Until the end of your next turn, your speed increases by 10 feet and you have advantage on Strength-based ability checks.
If you reduce a creature to 0 hit points during this time, you can immediately move up to 20 feet as a free action without provoking opportunity attacks.

description.p: Kraken’s Influence (Passive). The gauntlet subtly alters the battlefield, instilling fear in lesser foes.

ul.li: Creatures of CR 2 or lower within 30 feet of you must make a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened for 1 minute whenever you use a damaging ability from the gauntlet. They can repeat the saving throw at the end of their turns.
Allies within range gain a morale boost, receiving a +2 bonus to saving throws against fear effects.

description.p: Curse: Abyssal Hunger. The gauntlet is infused with the wrath of a long-forgotten abyssal entity and does not relinquish its power without a price.

ul.li: Life-Leeching Strain: Each time you use Abyssal Descent, you must make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or take 3d10 necrotic damage. This damage cannot be avoided or reduced.

Unrelenting Will: The gauntlet occasionally acts of its own accord, compelling you to strike targets or leap into danger. When you roll initiative, roll a d10. On a roll of 1, you immediately move toward the nearest enemy and attempt an attack on your first turn without using a bonus action.

setters.set: gauntlet, abyssal, kraken, force, shockwave, cursed

description.p: Your heart burns with unwavering faith. (Part of the Grandmaster’s Aegis.)

ul.li: Bonus: +2 bonus to AC (in addition to the armor’s base AC), and resistance to necrotic and radiant damage.
When you are struck by a melee attack, the attacker takes radiant damage equal to your proficiency bonus.
Once per short rest, as a reaction when you are hit by an attack, you can reduce the damage by 1d10 + your Constitution modifier.

description.p: Visual: Etched with runes that glow like sunlight over a horizon, with a central crest showing two angelic wings guarding a sun.

Set Bonus: The Grandmaster Ascendant. The full power of the Aegis awakens when all 5 pieces (Radiant Helm of Clarity, Chestplate of the Dawn, Gauntlets of Divine Might, Greaves of Swift Dawn, Cloak of the Morning Star) are worn while attuned to Dawnweaver:

ul.li: Gain +2 AC and +2 to all saving throws.
You emit a 30 ft aura of light. Allies inside gain resistance to necrotic damage and advantage on saving throws vs fear and charm.

Once per long rest, you can enter the Form of the Dawnbringer for 1 minute: you gain flight (80 ft), advantage on attack rolls, and your weapon attacks deal +2d6 radiant damage. You emit bright light in a 60 ft radius; darkness (magical or not) cannot exist within it. At the start of each of your turns, all fiends and undead within 30 ft take 10 radiant damage (no save). When the form ends, you regain HP equal to half your max.

description.p: The Grandmaster’s Aegis was crafted by the Solar Smith Seraphael as a twin to Dawnweaver, meant to be worn by the chosen champion who would lead the celestial armies against the Abyss. Few have ever borne the full set; those who did became legends whose names are sung in temples.

description.p: Massive Impact. When you hit a creature with this hammer, it takes an additional 3d10 force damage, and creatures of smaller size must make a DC 18 Strength saving throw or be launched 10 feet per point of damage dealt in a random direction.
Kinetic Charge (Reload Mechanic). The hammer’s explosive power is fueled by Titan Pebbles—small but unnaturally dense magical stones. It comes with 3 Titan Pebbles.

ul.li: Each Kinetic Charge Attack (special attack action) expends one Titan Pebble, creating a shockwave that deals 8d10 thunder damage in a 30-foot radius (DC 18 Constitution saving throw for half damage; creatures that fail are knocked prone).
Reloading Titan Pebbles takes 1 minute per pebble, as they must be carefully placed into the hammer’s absurdly convoluted mechanism.

description.p: Pebble Mishap. If you roll a natural 1 on an attack, roll a d6 to determine the malfunction:

tr.td: d6
Malfunction
Misfire! The hammer does nothing, but the pebble explodes in your hands, dealing 4d6 thunder damage to you.
Backblast! You are launched 20 feet backwards and must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or land prone.
Power Surge! The hammer activates twice, causing an uncontrollable 40-foot shockwave, knocking you prone and launching all creatures within 40 feet 20 feet outward.

description.p: Impractically Heavy. The hammer weighs 150 lb. Wielding it reduces your movement speed by 10 feet unless you have a Strength of 20 or higher.
“It’s just a little hammer with a little pebble.” — A fool before being obliterated

description.p: This deep green emerald shimmers with a faint, eerie glow when held up to the light. When attuned, it grants the user darkvision up to 60 feet and the ability to see through magical darkness. Its rarity and utility in both combat and stealth make it highly sought after by rogues and spellcasters alike.
A grotesque helm with a shifting, tooth-filled mouth.

ul.li: When you reduce a creature to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to 2d10 + your level.
As a bonus action, you can consume a corpse within 5 feet of you to regain 3d8 hit points.
Once per day, you can cast vampiric touch. For you, it requires no concentration and lasts 1 minute.

setters.set: helm, helmet, maw, feast, temporary hit points, vampiric touch

description.p: A thick, fleshy collar fused with jagged teeth on the inside. It occasionally swallows nothing.

ul.li: You have resistance to necrotic damage.

When you deal melee damage, you can force the target to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, you tear vitality from it, dealing an extra 2d8 necrotic damage and regaining hit points equal to that amount. You can use this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all uses when you finish a long rest.

When a creature dies within 10 feet of you, you can use your reaction to consume its essence. You gain 2d10 temporary hit points and a +1 bonus to attack rolls for 1 minute (this bonus stacks, up to +3).
If a creature dies within 10 feet of you and you do not consume it, you take 3d6 psychic damage.

At the start of combat, make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, you are driven to feed obsessively: you must move toward the nearest wounded creature each turn, and if you are adjacent to a creature below half its hit points, you must attack it.
If you go a full day without consuming a creature’s essence, you gain 1 level of exhaustion and have disadvantage on all attack rolls until you feed again.
If you consume essence 3 turns in a row, you enter a frenzy: you gain advantage on melee attacks, but you must attack every turn, prioritizing the nearest creature (including allies).

description.p: This imposing longsword has a mirror-like blade that gleams with an aura of self-confidence. The hilt is ornately decorated with gold and silver, and the pommel features a gemstone that seems to pulse with a faint, self-assured glow. Wielding the Sword of the Ego makes the bearer feel invincible.
Magical Weapon. The Sword of the Ego grants a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it.

Aura of Confidence. While attuned to this weapon, the wielder has advantage on Charisma checks (Intimidation and Persuasion) but disadvantage on Wisdom checks (Insight) and saving throws against being charmed or frightened.

Prideful Strike. Once per short rest, the wielder can declare a Prideful Strike before making an attack roll. On a hit, the attack deals an extra 2d6 psychic damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or be compelled to speak truthfully for the next minute. However, if the attack misses, the wielder becomes blinded by their own ego until the end of their next turn (blinded condition).

This unique longbow has a whimsical design with candy-like decorations on its limbs and a glossy, colorful finish that resembles a sweet treat. The bowstring is made from an unusual material that hums faintly, like a distant tune.

Every time you make an attack with this bow, you must say "Mmm, I'm eating, bro!" (or something similar). If you do, the arrow flies with surprising speed and accuracy, granting a +1 bonus to attack rolls.

Sugar Rush. Once per day, you can fire an arrow that bursts into a cloud of sweet-smelling mist upon impact, creating an area of Sugar Rush within a 10-foot radius. Creatures in the area must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or become hyperactive, gaining advantage on Dexterity checks and disadvantage on Wisdom checks for 1 minute.
Curse. If you fail to say the magic words when attacking, your next attack roll is made with disadvantage as the bow emits a loud, obnoxious chewing sound.
A tattered black cloak that seems to absorb light.
While wearing this cloak, you have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, and you can cast invisibility once per day.
Curse. Unknown.
A small black-red eye.
You have truesight out to a range of 30 feet.

Curse. The wearer is cursed with the Eye of True Sight. They are constantly aware of the presence of invisible or hidden creatures, which imposes disadvantage on Perception checks due to overwhelming sensory input. Additionally, they are unable to avert their gaze, giving them disadvantage on saving throws against gaze attacks (such as a basilisk's petrifying gaze).
Curse Removal Price: 3,500 gp.

An attack with this arrow grants advantage to the next attack roll made against the target. Additionally, the target emits 3 meters (10 feet) of dim light and loses all benefits from invisibility, if applicable, for 1 minute.
An arrow strike negates all effects that would heal the target and imposes disadvantage on all Strength and Dexterity saving throws for 1 minute.

This masterfully crafted longbow is forged from a blend of mystical wood and infused with arcane metals. Runes representing the forces of fire, ice, and other elements glow faintly along its limbs, shimmering with the power of the arrows it holds. The grip is wrapped in supple, black dragonhide, providing a firm hold and a sense of control over the bow’s immense power. The bow resonates with energy, and when drawn, the string crackles with potential.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls made with this bow.

ul.li: Range: 150/600 feet
Damage: 2d8 piercing + special effects based on arrow type
Special (Elemental Arrows): This bow is designed to store and unleash the following enchanted arrows: Fire, Cold, Acid, Lightning, Thunder, Radiant, Necrotic, Force, and Psychic.

description.p: Elemental Arrow Slots (9 Slots). The bow has 9 dedicated slots for storing each type of magical arrow. Once an arrow is placed into the corresponding slot, it can be drawn and fired from the bow. You can freely choose which type of arrow to shoot when making an attack. Each arrow has a different effect based on its element.

Arcane Charge (3/day). As a bonus action, you can activate the Arcane Charge ability of the bow. For the next minute, any elemental arrow fired from the bow deals an additional 1d8 damage of its respective type.

Harmonic Resonance. Once per long rest, the wielder can draw upon the elemental forces within the bow to fire an Elemental Barrage. The archer selects three different types of arrows, drawing and firing them in rapid succession as part of a single attack action. Each arrow strikes a different target of the wielder's choice within range.

Curse of the Elements. While this bow grants great power, it carries a burden. After attuning to the bow, the wielder becomes vulnerable to elemental damage (fire, cold, acid, lightning, and thunder). This vulnerability lasts until the attunement is broken.

description.p: Upon impact, the arrow inflicts an additional 2d8 fire damage. Any flammable object hit by this arrow ignites if it isn't being worn or carried.

A creature struck by this arrow has its speed reduced to 0. At the end of its turn, it regains 3 meters of movement speed. It continues to regain 3 meters of all available movement speeds at the end of each subsequent turn.

An arrow hit causes the target's armor to weaken at the point of contact. The target suffers a -1 reduction to AC. If the target's armor is natural, this effect lasts for 1 minute. If the armor is made of non-magical organic material or metals, the effect is permanent. A creature can suffer a cumulative maximum loss of 2 to their AC from these arrows.

A creature hit by this arrow is enveloped in crackling electricity that leaps to another creature of your choice within 4 meters. The secondary target must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d6 lightning damage on a failure or half as much on a success. If the initially hit creature is wearing metal armor, the saving throw increases to DC 17.
The impact of this arrow generates a thunderous boom audible over 30 meters. Each creature within 1 meter of the target takes 1d6 thunder damage.
A hit from this arrow deals an additional 2 force damage and pushes the target back 4 meters.

A creature struck by this arrow is tormented by crippling voices. Until the end of their turn, the creature is frightened of the archer. For 1 minute, the creature also suffers disadvantage on Wisdom saving throws.

Dawnweaver is a celestial weapon, forged in the heavens and blessed by the gods. In its sword form, it is a long, radiant silver blade adorned with glowing holy symbols and runes. The hilt is wrapped in white leather with golden stitching, and the pommel features a large gemstone that emits a divine glow. When commanded, the blade transforms into a segmented whip connected by chains of pure, celestial light.
Weapon Type: Longsword (versatile), with a secondary whip form.

ul.li: Level 9 - Radiant Edge: In sword form, Dawnweaver deals an extra 2d6 radiant damage on a hit. Against fiends and undead, this damage increases to 3d6. The sword emits bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet.

Level 10 - Divine Whip Form: As a bonus action, the wielder can transform the sword into a whip form. In this form, the weapon gains the reach property (adding 10 feet to its range) and deals 1d8 slashing damage plus 2d6 radiant damage on a hit. It can also be used to disarm or grapple opponents, granting advantage on such attempts.

Level 11 - Holy Smite: Once per long rest, the wielder can unleash a powerful smite, dealing an additional 6d6 radiant damage and forcing all creatures of evil alignment within a 30-foot radius to make a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened for 1 minute. Creatures that succeed on the save are immune to this effect for 24 hours.

Level 12 - Divine Reach: You can use your bonus action to change your sword to a whip. While in whip form, Dawnweaver can extend its reach to 20 feet. The wielder can attack enemies or interact with objects up to this range, using the whip as an extension of their arm.

Level 13 - Celestial Guard: The wielder gains a +2 bonus to AC and saving throws against spells cast by fiends or undead. If the wielder drops to 0 hit points while wielding Dawnweaver, they are instead reduced to 1 hit point and gain temporary hit points equal to their level. This effect can trigger once per day.
Level 14 - Blessing of the Dawn: Dawnweaver grants resistance to necrotic damage and the ability to cast lesser restoration once per short rest.

Level 15 - Wings of the Dawn: While attuned to and wielding Dawnweaver, the wielder sprouts golden, radiant wings. The wings grant a flying speed of 60 feet and emit a warm, golden light. The wings are durable but ethereal, allowing the wielder to fly and maneuver with grace. The wielder can retract or manifest the wings as a bonus action. If the wielder is knocked unconscious or drops the sword, the wings dissipate until they recover or reclaim the weapon.

description.p: Appearance. In sword form, Dawnweaver is a brilliant, shining longsword with runes etched along the blade that pulse with radiant energy. The crossguard is shaped like angelic wings, and the gem in the pommel glows with divine light. In whip form, the sword segments into radiant pieces connected by chains of celestial energy, becoming a glowing whip that can extend and retract at the wielder's command. When the wings manifest, they appear as a pair of large, golden, feathered wings that shimmer with divine light, allowing the wielder to soar through the skies.

Dawnweaver is more than just a weapon—it is a symbol of hope and divine justice. Forged in the celestial forges of the Upper Planes, it was a gift from the gods to the mortal realm, meant to be wielded by a champion of light in the darkest of times. Legends say that it was last wielded by a great hero who led an army against a host of fiends, their golden wings shining like the dawn. The sword chooses its wielder carefully, requiring both strength and righteousness to unlock its full potential.

Relentless Pursuit: When reduced to 0 HP, you instead drop to 1 HP. Until the end of your next turn, your movement speed increases by 20 feet.
Survival Instinct (Slay a Beast): Gain advantage on initiative rolls.
Beast’s Tenacity (Slay a Monster): You gain advantage on Strength and Dexterity saving throws while below half HP.
Ambush Sense (Slay Nyx, the Flickering Terror): You can’t be surprised while conscious.
Unbreakable (Slay a Legendary Foe): If you would be knocked unconscious while at 1 HP, you can make a Constitution saving throw to remain standing.
Reckless Retaliation (Slay a Warrior): If an enemy within 5 feet drops you to 1 HP, you can use your reaction to make an unarmed strike against them.

description.p: A dark silver ring with shifting runes that pulse faintly with magical energy.
Primary Effect. Every time an ally within 30 feet fails two death saving throws, the wearer regains all expended spell slots up to 6th level instantly.
Recharge Effect. At the start of every day, the ring randomly gains a new effect from the following:

ul.li: 1. Soulfire Surge: Your fire spells ignore resistance and deal +1d8 damage.
2. Temporal Echo: Once per long rest, you can recast a spell without expending a slot (must be of 5th level or lower).
3. Void Shield: Gain advantage on all saving throws against magic until the next dawn.
4. Essence Siphon: When you deal damage with a spell, heal for half the damage dealt (max 25 HP per spell).

ul.li: Primary Effect: If you fail two death saving throws, your attacks for the next minute automatically crit on a roll of 18–20.
Secondary Effect: When firing at a creature below half HP, you can expend an arrow to summon a spectral beast that deals 2d8 extra radiant damage.
Bonus: If a favored enemy is reduced to 0 HP, you can make one additional attack as a reaction.

Secondary Effect: Once per long rest, you can absorb an attack that would drop you to 0 HP, taking no damage and healing for 2d10 + your Constitution modifier.
Bonus: While wielding this shield, enemies have disadvantage on opportunity attacks against you.

description.p: A shield crackling with divine lightning, a gift from the storm gods to their chosen champion.

ul.li: Primary Effect: Once per long rest, if you fail two death saving throws, lightning strikes you from the heavens, restoring you to full HP and dealing 6d10 lightning damage to all enemies within 20 feet.
Secondary Effect: Once per long rest, when you or an ally within 10 feet is reduced to 0 HP, you can restore them to half their max HP instantly.
Bonus: When casting call lightning, you can summon two bolts instead of one, targeting different creatures.

description.p: This elegant rapier is forged from black adamantine, its blade adorned with silver veining that glimmers faintly, resembling moonlight weaving through a spider’s web. The hilt is shaped like intertwining spider legs, with an amethyst set into the pommel, glowing softly with a purplish light. Though clearly of Drow design, the rapier welcomes any skilled wielder to master its unique abilities.
Magical Weapon. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this weapon.

Shadow Cloning (3/day). As a bonus action, you can summon up to 3 shadowy clones of yourself within 30 feet. These clones appear as perfect replicas of you, shrouded in a misty, ethereal darkness. They last for up to 1 minute or until dismissed as a bonus action.

ul.li: The clones cannot deal damage or physically interact with objects but feel real to the touch. If a creature touches a clone, it must succeed on a DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) check to recognize it as an illusion. On a failure, the creature believes the clone is real.
The clones mimic your movements but can be commanded to move independently as a bonus action.

description.p: Shadow Blink Strike. When a creature ends its turn within 5 feet of one of your clones, you can use your reaction to teleport to the clone’s location and make one melee weapon attack with the rapier. This attack catches your target off-guard, dealing an additional 1d6 psychic damage if it hits. The teleportation and strike occur simultaneously, allowing you to exploit the confusion caused by the clones.
Illusory Reality. The clones are highly convincing, giving off warmth and weight when touched, further adding to their believability.
Cloak of Shadows. While attuned to this weapon, you can cast the darkness spell once per long rest without expending a spell slot. The darkness does not hinder your ability to see within it.
Versatile Legacy. Though inspired by the shadowy artistry of Drow craftsmanship, this weapon is open to mastery by any wielder skilled enough to channel its power.

This ancient book is bound in cracked, blackened leather, with faded, silver runes etched along the spine. The pages seem to shift and ripple like liquid ink, constantly rearranging themselves as if the knowledge within resists being read. An aura of dark magic can be felt when holding the tome, and it feels heavier than it should, as though burdened by its forbidden knowledge.
Forbidden Knowledge. Once per day, the user can learn a necromancy spell from the tome that they do not currently know. This spell can be cast once without using a spell slot.
Aging Curse. Each time a spell is learned from the tome, the user ages by one year. This effect cannot be reversed by any means.

A black obsidian gemstone, polished to a mirror-like sheen, rests at the center of this amulet, surrounded by an intricate frame of twisted silver. Tiny skulls and bones are subtly carved into the metalwork, and when held, the wearer can hear faint, ghostly whispers. The amulet's surface is always cold to the touch, and mist seems to swirl around it in the faintest light.

Soul Communication. The wearer can use an action to cast speak with dead without using a spell slot, with unlimited uses. However, each use beyond the first each day has a 10% cumulative chance of attracting hostile undead to the wearer’s location.

Command Undead. Three times per day, the wearer can attempt to control an undead creature within 30 feet. The creature can make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 15) to resist. If the creature fails, it follows the commands of the amulet's wearer for 1 hour or until it takes damage.

setters.set: amulet, undead, speak with dead, crypt

description.p: This cursed goblet is forged from tarnished silver, encrusted with large, dark black diamonds. Streaks of dried blood permanently stain its interior, and faint runes of sacrifice are etched along its rim. The goblet feels unnaturally cold when held, and any liquid poured into it seems to darken as though tainted by the goblet’s curse.

Drain Vitality. When the user drinks from the goblet, they gain resistance to all damage types for 1 minute. Each round this power is active, a living creature within 30 feet of the user takes 1d6 necrotic damage. The closest creatures are affected first, and creatures reduced to 0 hit points by this effect have their life force completely drained, instantly killing them.

Blood Bond. If a creature is killed by the goblet's life-draining effect, the user can opt to bind the soul of the deceased to the goblet. This grants the user an additional use of the goblet’s power per day but at the cost of permanent disadvantage on all saving throws against necrotic damage.

This small, handheld mirror is framed in ancient bones inscribed with faintly glowing runes. The glass is cloudy, as if obscured by mist, yet when someone gazes into it with intent, images of the past begin to materialize. The bone handle is warm to the touch, and when in use, the runes glow faintly with an eerie light.

Scry the Past. Once per day, the user can focus on a visible location or object while holding the mirror. The mirror shows a significant event that occurred in the past at that location or involving that object. The vision lasts for up to 1 minute.

Memory Echo. When a past event is viewed using the mirror, the user can attempt to interact with the memory to learn more details or uncover hidden truths. This requires a successful DC 17 Intelligence check. On a failure, the mirror breaks.

element.name: Abbados, Battle Axe of the Underworld

description.p: This imposing battleaxe is forged from dark iron and obsidian, with its twin blades resembling the wings of a dark creature. Faint necrotic energy crackles along its edges, and the haft is wrapped in blackened leather. The pommel is shaped like a skull, its eyes glowing faintly with a cold, blue light. When swung, the axe emits a low, ominous hum, as though it were slicing through the very fabric of life itself.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit with an attack from this weapon, the target takes an additional 2d8 necrotic damage.
While attuned to this magic weapon, your Strength score increases by 2, even over 20.

This weapon has 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding it, you may spend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells: false life (1–5 charges, casting the spell at a level equal to the number of charges), inflict wounds (2 charges), and blight (5 charges).

setters.set: Abbados, Battle Axe of the Underworld

description.p: This tall, elegant staff is carved from pristine white wood and adorned with intricate arcane symbols. At its peak rests a sapphire that glows faintly with magical energy, hinting at the immense power contained within. The staff pulses with the creativity of the arcane, allowing its wielder to craft magnificent structures and manipulate the very fabric of space.

Effect. The staff grants a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the DC of your spell saving throws. While holding the staff, you can cast Mordenkainen’s magnificent mansion and teleport once per long rest without expending a spell slot.

Special Power. Once per month, the wielder can use the staff to create an Arcane Fortress, a grand magical structure designed entirely by the user. The fortress remains in existence for 7 days or until dispelled.

Forged from the very essence of a raging storm, this longsword crackles with arcs of lightning that dance along its blade. The sword hums with the power of the tempest, its soft blue glow illuminating its surroundings like the calm before a storm. The wielder of this weapon commands the fury of the skies.

Effect. This +3 longsword grants a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls. Upon hitting a target, it deals an additional 3d8 lightning damage. While attuned to the Blade of the Eternal Tempest, you gain resistance to both lightning and thunder damage.

Special Power. Once per day, the sword’s wielder can summon a storm to call down lightning bolts as per the call lightning spell, cast at 9th level. This does not require a spell slot or concentration.

Forged from polished ivory and etched with necromantic runes, this ring allows its wearer to control skeletons within a 60-foot radius. Necromancers covet this item for its ability to easily summon and command minions, while collectors prize it for its dark aesthetic and rare power.

This twisted, blackened staff hums with malevolent energy. At its head is a skull encased in arcane runes that glow faintly in the dark. The staff allows its wielder to cast necromantic spells with greater efficiency, reducing the spell slots needed by one for necromancy-related magic. This relic has been passed down by generations of dark sorcerers, increasing its allure.

This ornate chest is covered in swirling runes and carved depictions of spirits being bound in servitude. It offers an extra-dimensional storage space, capable of holding vast amounts of items without increasing weight. The chest is magically attuned to a soul, preventing anyone else from opening it unless they know the passphrase.

These crystals glow faintly with an inner light, each one attuned to a different school of magic. Commonly used as spell components or for arcane research, their value depends on the type of magic they resonate with. They are most often found embedded in ancient ruins.
Gold Value: 50 gp each.

A leather pouch filled with rare herbs such as Ghostroot and Nightshade, both of which are crucial for potion-making and rituals involving poison or necromancy. While common among experienced herbalists, the rarity of some herbs makes this a valuable find.

Fragile, yellowed parchments that show ancient territories, forgotten routes, and potential treasure locations. Some of the scrolls contain fragmented spells or incantations that may require further research to decipher fully. Their value could increase significantly if sold to an archaeologist or wizard.

These finely carved bone dice are etched with intricate symbols and sigils. Not only are they a prized possession for collectors, but they are also rumored to have mystical properties, possibly influencing fate when used in games or certain rituals.

element.name: The Hand of the Endless Abyss

description.p: A single black gauntlet that looks as though it’s forged from shadow and obsidian. Delicate runes writhe along its surface like living ink, occasionally forming the outline of reaching tentacles. It feels unnaturally heavy when worn. Once attuned, it bonds to the user, fusing its shadowy substance with their flesh.

ul.li: Snare: As an action, shadowy tendrils lash out from the gauntlet toward a creature you can see within 30 feet. The target must succeed on a DC 17 Strength saving throw or be grappled and restrained by the tendrils until the start of your next turn. You can use this ability 3 times per long rest.
Pull: If a creature is restrained by the tendrils, you can use a bonus action to pull it up to 15 feet closer to you.
Silent Utility: The tendrils can latch onto surfaces to help you swing across gaps or climb.

Leeching Touch: You can place your hand on a creature (or your own body) and drain life force to restore hit points. As an action, choose one: heal yourself or an ally for 4d8 hit points; or Drain an unwilling creature, which must make a DC 17 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 4d8 necrotic damage, and you heal for half the amount dealt.

Overheal Corruption: Each time you use this ability, roll a d6. On a roll of 1, the gauntlet begins siphoning your life force as punishment. You take 2d10 necrotic damage that cannot be reduced or avoided.

description.p: As an action, you can make a melee weapon attack using the gauntlet. On a hit, the gauntlet deals 4d10 force damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 17 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone. If this ability is used against a creature below 50 hit points, the tendrils crush the creature outright, reducing it to 0 hit points as its body implodes. You can use this ability once per long rest.
Curse: The Gauntlet's Price. The Hand of the Endless Abyss exerts a constant toll on its wielder, symbolizing its overwhelming power:

ul.li: Crushing Grip: Each time you use one of the gauntlet’s abilities, make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the gauntlet’s shadowy power constricts, dealing 2d6 bludgeoning damage and reducing your Dexterity by 1. If your Dexterity reaches 0, your hand is completely crushed and unusable, requiring regenerate or similar magic to restore. Removing the gauntlet before fully paying the price requires a greater restoration or a powerful ritual, as it fuses more tightly with its wielder over time.

Eternal Bond: If the gauntlet fully crushes your hand (Dexterity reduced to 0), you must make a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, you become possessed by the gauntlet’s abyssal will, driven to use its powers recklessly, even against allies.

Mark of the Abyss: While attuned, your veins blacken slightly, and faint whispers echo in your mind when you sleep. Overuse of the gauntlet might result in permanent, visible corruption, such as shadowed skin or semi-visible tendrils that coil around your arm.

description.p: Attunement: Abyssal Trial. To attune to the Hand, the wielder must survive a vision of the abyss itself. Shadows engulf them as they are faced with manifestations of their fears and regrets. The user must pass three Wisdom saving throws (DC 16) or be temporarily consumed by despair, reducing all saving throws by -2 for the next 24 hours. They must also grapple with the gauntlet's abyssal will. A failed Charisma (Intimidation or Persuasion) contest allows the Hand to scar their mind with shadowy visions, taking 2d10 psychic damage.

A dark, crystalline amulet resembling an entwined vine and chain. Within its core, a faintly glowing orb pulsates with a rhythmic, heartbeat-like light. The chain itself is unnervingly warm, and when worn, the user feels a faint connection to those around them—as though invisible threads bind their fates together.

1. Symbiotic Bond. The amulet can forge ethereal links between the wearer and other creatures, transferring benefits and debuffs across these connections. The wearer can create up to 3 bonds at a time (or sever them as a bonus action).

ul.li: Link to Allies: As a bonus action, the wearer can bond to an ally within 60 feet. Any positive effects on the wearer (such as buffs, spell effects, or resistances) are shared with bonded allies. For example, if the wearer has bless or resistance to fire, so do their bonded allies. Bonded allies gain a +2 bonus to saving throws while linked.

Link to Enemies: As an action, the wearer can bond to an enemy within 60 feet. The enemy automatically loses one beneficial buff or condition (chosen by the wearer) each round they remain bonded. For example, the amulet can strip a target’s haste or shield of faith spell. The wearer can redistribute the stolen buff to themselves or a bonded ally. If no valid target exists, the buff dissipates. Enemies bonded this way suffer disadvantage on saving throws against spells or abilities cast by the wearer.

description.p: 2. Curse of Parity. The wearer can manipulate the balance between their allies and enemies. As an action, the wearer can:

ul.li: Debilitating Bond: For 1 minute, bonded enemies gain vulnerability to one damage type of the wearer’s choice (e.g., fire, radiant, etc.), chosen when the ability is activated.

Sympathetic Feedback: Whenever a bonded enemy is affected by a harmful condition (such as being restrained, paralyzed, or blinded), the wearer can transfer the same condition to another bonded enemy as a reaction.

description.p: 3. Echo of Dominance. Once per long rest, the wearer can activate the amulet’s full power to reshape the battlefield for 3 turns:

ul.li: All bonded allies within 60 feet automatically succeed on saving throws against spells or magical effects.
All bonded enemies automatically fail their saving throws against the wearer’s spells or magical effects.
The wearer can link themselves to up to 5 targets during this effect (instead of the usual 3).

description.p: Curse: Chain of the Overmind. The amulet exerts control over its wearer, much like its connections bind others:

ul.li: Parasitic Strain: For every bond the wearer creates, they suffer 1d8 psychic damage per round, per active bond. This damage cannot be resisted or avoided.

Loss of Identity: After 24 hours of continuous attunement, the wearer has disadvantage on all Wisdom saving throws and Insight checks. After 2 days, the wearer must succeed on a DC 18 Charisma saving throw each dawn or permanently lose 1 point of Charisma. If their Charisma reaches 0, their mind fractures entirely, and they become an NPC under the DM’s control, enslaved to the amulet’s will.

Forced Bonds: The amulet occasionally forges bonds of its own accord, typically at inopportune moments. At the DM’s discretion, the amulet may link the wearer to unintended allies or enemies, creating chaos in combat.

description.p: Attunement: Linking Ceremony. The user meditates in complete silence while wearing the amulet, allowing their thoughts to flow outward into the connections of fate. The ritual requires them to forge symbolic connections to allies and enemies through roleplay or illusion, which could reflect their moral alignment. The user must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, they experience uncontrolled emotional echoes from others around them, taking 1d8 psychic damage for each ally and enemy linked in their mind.

A massive, ancient tome bound in leathery skin with a shifting, pulsating surface. Its spine is covered in faintly glowing runes, and its pages ripple as though alive, whispering in an unidentifiable language. When held, the grimoire feels warm and heavy, almost as if it’s breathing. The wielder senses an unsettling, watchful presence.
Weapon Type: Counts as a ranged spellcasting weapon (uses the wielder’s spellcasting ability modifier for attack rolls), but it attacks by unleashing eldritch pages and effects.

1. Eldritch Flurry. As an action, you can open the grimoire and command its pages to lash out at a target within 30 feet. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 3d12 force damage, and the eldritch energy clings to them, reducing their movement speed by 10 feet until the end of their next turn. You can use this feature three times per long rest.
2. Shape the Unknown. As a bonus action, you can speak the grimoire’s command word to change its form, activating one of the following:

ul.li: Shield of Words: Gain a +2 bonus to AC until the start of your next turn.

Binding Script: As an action, target a creature within 30 feet. It must succeed on a DC 18 Strength saving throw or be restrained for 1 minute. A restrained creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of its turns.

Chaos Script: Tear a page from the book as an action and throw it at a point within 60 feet. All creatures within a 10-foot radius sphere must succeed on a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw or take 4d10 force damage and be knocked prone.

description.p: 3. Infinite Knowledge. As a bonus action, you can consult the grimoire to gain advantage on any Arcana, History, or Investigation check. For every check you make using the grimoire, there is a 10% chance the whispers will grow overwhelming, causing you to suffer 2d8 psychic damage.
Curse: Hunger of the Tome. The Living Grimoire is not a weapon—it is a living being:

ul.li: Eldritch Parasite: Each time you use one of the grimoire’s abilities, you must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or lose 1d6 hit points that cannot be healed until the next long rest.
Maddening Whispers: Each night, while attuned, you must succeed on a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or gain one level of exhaustion.

The Final Page: The grimoire’s final ability remains locked unless the wielder sacrifices 10 hit points permanently to unlock it. Once unlocked, the user can cast disintegrate (DC 18) once per day, using the book as the spellcasting focus. Using this ability has a 50% chance of summoning a hostile extraplanar creature (DM’s choice) that seeks to reclaim the grimoire.

description.p: The grimoire is sentient, communicating with the wielder telepathically. It refers to itself as "Archivist" and claims to hold the sum of all forbidden knowledge in the multiverse.

Attunement: The Question of Knowledge. The tome presents the wielder with an esoteric riddle tied to ancient or forbidden knowledge. The user must attempt to solve it through Arcana, History, or Investigation (DC 20). Success unlocks the bond. Failure results in the grimoire feeding on the user's vitality, dealing 2d12 psychic damage. It will not allow another attunement attempt until seven days have passed or significant new lore is uncovered.

setters.set: grimoire, book, sentient, archivist, vault, cursed

description.p: This ancient hourglass, forged from shimmering gold and set with rare gemstones, contains swirling sands of time that defy all natural laws.

Rewind Fate (1/Day). As a reaction to being hit by an attack or failing a saving throw, the wielder can turn the hourglass, rewinding time to the start of their turn in the current round. All actions taken since that turn are undone, but the user retains knowledge of what occurred. Any effects caused to others are reverted, and they do not recall the events that were undone.
Sands of Vision (3/Day). As an action, the wielder can cast divination or legend lore up to three times per day without expending a spell slot.
Temporal Shield (1/Day). As a bonus action, the hourglass creates a shield of flowing time around the wielder, granting immunity to all damage types for one round.

Curse: Temporal Echo. Each time the wielder uses one of the hourglass's abilities, there is a 10% chance (roll of 90–100 on a d100) that a temporal echo of themselves from an alternate timeline is summoned. This echo is hostile and seeks to eliminate the user, believing them to be an imposter. The echo has the same stats and abilities as the wielder and disappears after 1d4 + 1 rounds if not destroyed.

setters.set: hourglass, time, divination, vault unveiling, cursed

set.name: attunement
set.addition: by a spellcaster

description.p: A chain made of blackened steel, with faint, glowing runes etched into every link. When held, it feels unnaturally heavy, as though it carries the weight of countless lifetimes.
While attuned, this chain grants the wearer immense resilience:

ul.li: +2 to AC and saving throws.
Immunity to exhaustion and aging effects.
You can use an action to bind the chain around yourself, becoming immune to all damage for 1 round (once per long rest).

description.p: Curse. Each day the wearer is attuned to this item, they lose one hit die permanently, representing their life force being consumed. When the wearer has no hit dice left, they die, and their soul is absorbed into the chain, becoming one of the voices bound to its power.

A large, aged tome with a blackened leather cover. The book is secured with an ornate lock in the shape of the Ring of Spell Stealing, which acts as the only key. When the ring is inserted, the book emits a faint, eerie hum, resonating with arcane energy. Runes swirl briefly across its surface before settling into stillness.

ul.li: The Spell Steal Book works in tandem with the Ring of Spell Stealing. When the wearer of the ring absorbs a spell, they can transfer the spell into this book as an action.

Once the spell is in the book, it can be transcribed into the user’s spellbook (if they are a wizard) or used as a one-time casting for non-wizards. Casting the stored spell from the book consumes the stored spell and requires no spell slot.
The book can hold up to 10 spells at any given time. If full, a new spell can overwrite an old one.

description.p: Requires attunement to both the ring and the book, linking the two items as a set.

setters.set: book, spells, ring of spell stealing, vault unveiling

set.name: attunement
set.addition: together with the Ring of Spell Stealing

description.p: A heavy, iron-bound ledger with pages made of tarnished gold foil. The cover bears the engraving of a skeletal hand clutching a coin. The book feels unnaturally cold to the touch, and faint whispers of "payment due" can be heard when it’s opened.

Tally of Power. As an action, the user can record a creature’s name in the ledger (the creature must be within 60 feet and visible). The next time the creature casts a spell, deals damage, or regains hit points, the ledger collects a tax equal to 10% of the effect (rounded up). For damage or healing, this tax is deducted directly from the amount. For spell slots, the creature must roll a d20; on a 10 or lower, the slot is expended but the spell fizzles.

The ledger can record up to 20 names at a time. A recorded name can only be removed when the target is reduced to 0 hit points, willingly pays a fee of 500 gp, or the user erases it using a wish spell.

Curse. Each name recorded adds 1d6 psychic damage to all saving throws the user makes while attuned to the ledger. If the ledger has 10 or more names, the user suffers disadvantage on all Wisdom and Charisma checks due to the haunting voices demanding payments from their mind.
Price: 6,000 gp (listed at 9,000 gp at the Vault Unveiling).

set.name: attunement
set.addition: by a creature that is not of chaotic alignment

element.name: The Mask of the Unseen Tyrant

description.p: Supreme Domination. The wearer can cast dominate monster (DC 20) twice per day, without requiring a spell slot. The effect lasts for 8 hours unless the target succeeds on a saving throw at the end of their turn (still made with disadvantage).

Aura of Subjugation. Creatures within 30 feet of the wearer must make a DC 18 Charisma saving throw or be unable to attack the wearer directly for 1 minute. Affected creatures can repeat the saving throw at the end of their turns.
Veil of Invisibility. The wearer can become invisible at will as a bonus action. This invisibility lasts until they attack, cast a spell, or remove the mask.

Heightened Charisma. The wearer’s Charisma score becomes 22 while attuned. If the score is already 22 or higher, they gain proficiency in Deception, Intimidation, and Persuasion (or expertise if already proficient).

Curse. The mask progressively deteriorates the wearer’s trust in others. Each day of attunement imposes a cumulative -1 penalty to Wisdom. After one week, the wearer becomes an NPC if they fail a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw, believing themselves to be a divine ruler and treating their allies as subjects or threats.

setters.set: mask, tyrant, domination, vault unveiling, cursed

description.p: A quill that shimmers with a glassy translucence, its edges fracturing light into dazzling, fleeting colors. It radiates an almost oppressive aura of precision and justice, with faint whispers of undeniable truths echoing around it when touched.

Reality Script. Once per day, you may use the quill to inscribe a sentence of no more than 20 words on a surface or in the air. The sentence must state a clear, verifiable truth or reality you wish to impose. For 24 hours, this truth becomes absolute and cannot be undone except by a wish spell or divine intervention. For example: "No one within the city walls can lie," or "The king is bound to obey his people's will." The truth affects reality itself, overriding laws, physics, or personal abilities.
Permanent Truth. Once per week, the user may write a sentence to permanently alter reality. However, the act destroys the quill in the process.
Detect Falsehood. The quill allows the user to cast zone of truth (DC 18, no concentration required) at will, with the zone being visible as a faint golden glow.
Aura of Honesty. While attuned, creatures within 15 feet of the user must succeed on a DC 16 Charisma saving throw to speak an intentional falsehood.

Curse. Every time the quill is used, the user must succeed on a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw or lose 1 point of Charisma permanently as the burden of reshaping reality corrodes their sense of identity and self-expression. If the user’s Charisma reaches 0, they become an automaton-like shell of their former self, compelled only to speak and enforce the truths they’ve written.

setters.set: quill, truth, reality, vault unveiling, cursed

description.p: This ornate golden crown is masterfully crafted, its delicate filigree framing a large, radiant opal that seems to pulse with an inner light. The opal glows with the faint whispers of celestial beings, imparting divine knowledge to its wearer.

Effect. While wearing the Crown of Celestial Insight, you gain proficiency in all Intelligence-based skills (Arcana, History, Investigation, Nature, Religion). Additionally, you can cast the legend lore spell once per long rest without expending a spell slot. Once per day, you may also cast true seeing without using a spell slot.

Special Power. Once per week, the wearer may ask a single question to a celestial entity as though casting the divination spell, receiving a direct answer without requiring material components or spell slots.

This shimmering platinum ring is topped with a crystal orb that rotates gently within its socket, glowing with the colors of shifting realities. The wearer is said to influence the very fabric of fate itself, bending possibilities in their favor.

Effect. Once per day, the wearer of this ring may reroll any die, and they must take the new result, regardless of the outcome. Additionally, the wearer may use the wish spell once, after which the ring crumbles to dust.

Special Power. The ring can absorb and hold up to three spells (up to 9th level) cast by another creature within 30 feet. The wearer can cast these stored spells at will as if they had prepared them, using the original spell level, DC, and spellcasting ability of the caster.
This silver amulet is shaped like an hourglass, with sand that constantly shifts and flows within, defying the laws of gravity. Those who wear this artifact hold dominion over fleeting moments.
Effect. Once per day, the wearer can cast time stop without using a spell slot. Additionally, the wearer may take one extra action on their turn once per long rest.

Special Power. Once per long rest, the wearer can rewind time by 6 seconds (1 round), forcing all creatures (except the wearer) to repeat their last turn exactly as it happened, while the wearer retains full knowledge of the original events.
Effect: Grants the ability to cast fireball (3rd level) once per day.
Appearance: A jagged, fiery rune that glows with an internal heat, even when etched into cold steel.

Sold by the Arcane Etcher in Mercia. Etching the rune into a non-magical item takes a day and costs an additional 500 gp. Two minor runes can be combined into one item for 1,000 gp (risking destabilization), and a rune's uses can be extended by +1 for 1,500 gp.
Effect: Allows the bearer to cast shield as a reaction, granting +5 to AC until the start of the next turn.
Appearance: A protective, spiraling symbol that glows faintly with a silver hue.

Sold by the Arcane Etcher in Mercia. Etching the rune into a non-magical item takes a day and costs an additional 500 gp. Two minor runes can be combined into one item for 1,000 gp (risking destabilization), and a rune's uses can be extended by +1 for 1,500 gp.
Effect: Allows the bearer to cast misty step (2nd level) once per day.
Appearance: A whirling, wind-like pattern that seems to shimmer and move as if alive.

Sold by the Arcane Etcher in Mercia. Etching the rune into a non-magical item takes a day and costs an additional 500 gp. Two minor runes can be combined into one item for 1,000 gp (risking destabilization), and a rune's uses can be extended by +1 for 1,500 gp.
Effect: Grants the ability to cast lightning bolt (3rd level) once per day.
Appearance: A jagged rune that crackles with static energy, occasionally sparking harmlessly.

Sold by the Arcane Etcher in Mercia. Etching the rune into a non-magical item takes a day and costs an additional 500 gp. Two minor runes can be combined into one item for 1,000 gp (risking destabilization), and a rune's uses can be extended by +1 for 1,500 gp.
Effect: Allows the bearer to cast cure wounds (2nd level) once per day.
Appearance: A smooth, flowing rune that glows with a soothing, pale green light.

Sold by the Arcane Etcher in Mercia. Etching the rune into a non-magical item takes a day and costs an additional 500 gp. Two minor runes can be combined into one item for 1,000 gp (risking destabilization), and a rune's uses can be extended by +1 for 1,500 gp.
Effect: Allows the bearer to cast invisibility (2nd level) once per day.
Appearance: A dark rune that absorbs light, giving the item a shadowy, ethereal appearance.

Gunblade Mechanism (The "Boom-Swing" System). This greatsword has an integrated break-action gunpowder chamber, which fires a round every time you swing—adding extra force to your attacks… and often throwing you backward.

ul.li: Gunblade Shot (Bonus Action, 4 rounds per long rest): After making an attack, you can choose to ignite the built-in gunpowder charge, launching an explosive round along the sword’s swing arc. Extra Damage: +1d12 thunder damage. Recoil Effect: Make a DC 14 Strength saving throw. On a fail, you are launched 10 feet backward and land prone. On a natural 1, the recoil dislocates your shoulder, giving -2 to attack rolls until a short rest.
Ammunition Type: Custom Barnaby Special Shells™ (see table).

description.p: The "Overcharge" Button. A red button on the hilt labeled "DO NOT PRESS". If pressed, the next swing deals double damage, recoil increases to 20 feet, and the wielder must make a DC 16 Constitution save or be temporarily deafened for 1 minute from the explosion.
Barnaby Special Shells™ (roll a d6 whenever you fire a Gunblade Shot):

Result
The GOOD One – Works as intended. +1d12 thunder damage. No mishaps. (How rare!)

description.p: Shell Types (roll a d6 whenever you fire the javelin):

Snare Mode (Special Attack, Bonus Action). Instead of dealing damage, you can attempt to clamp down on a creature within 10 feet. Auto-Spin Mode! – The staff violently spins the restrained target in place, dealing 1d6 bludgeoning damage per round but also makes it impossible to let go for 1d4 rounds.
Electrified Clamps! – The device sparks wildly, dealing 2d6 lightning damage to both you and the restrained creature.

ul.li: "Why Is It So Heavy?": Holding the staff reduces your movement speed by 5 feet.
"Where’s the Release Button?!": Releasing a snared enemy takes an action, unless you "solve the problem" by slamming them into something.
"Sometimes It Grabs Things It Shouldn’t.": If you roll a natural 1 while attacking, the weapon snaps shut on the nearest object (wall, chair, ally, your own arm, etc.).

description.p: Auto-Draw Mechanism™ (Because Manual Drawing is for Peasants). This bow does not require a normal draw. Instead, it has a clockwork-powered string system that launches arrows at high velocity. However… Barnaby’s engineering choices mean it’s completely unpredictable.
Firing Mode (every attack roll, roll a d6):

tr.td: d6
Result
String-Snap! – The bowstring snaps mid-shot, dealing 1d6 slashing damage to the wielder. The arrow falls 5 feet away from you. (Oops!)
Overcharged Shot! – The arrow fires at 3× velocity, increasing range to 600 ft and dealing 1d12 damage instead. However, you must make a DC 14 Strength save or be knocked prone from recoil.
Multi-Shot Mode! – The bow randomly fires 1d4 arrows at once. Pick different targets or send all into one enemy. (Does this waste ammo? Absolutely!)
Drunken Aim Mode! – The Auto-Draw system overcompensates, forcing the shot to curve wildly. Roll a d8 for a random direction adjustment.
Explosive Arrow! – Instead of a normal arrow, the bow somehow loads an explosive round (dealing 2d6 fire damage in a 10 ft radius). The wielder must roll a DC 14 Dexterity save or get singed as well.
Perfect Shot! – The bow actually works as intended. The attack automatically hits and deals maximum damage. (Barnaby is so proud!)

ul.li: "The Self-Tightening Bowstring": After every 5 shots, the bowstring tightens too much. If not manually adjusted (bonus action), the next shot has disadvantage.
"Backup Fire Mode": If the bowstring completely jams (rolling two natural 1s in a row), the bow has a spring-loaded emergency release that fires the wielder 10 feet backward.

"What’s This Button Do?": A mysterious button near the grip. Roll a d4: 1 = Nothing, 2 = Auto-fire mode (1d4 extra shots), 3 = Arrow turns into a homing chicken, 4 = The entire bow vibrates uncontrollably for 1 minute.
"Loud as Hell": Every shot makes a clanking, whirring, and sometimes explosive sound, removing all stealth advantages.
"Why Does It Keep Clicking?": Sometimes the Auto-Draw pretends to fire, but does nothing (roll a d20; on a 5 or lower, the shot just… doesn’t happen).
"Oh No, The Gears Are Stuck": If the wielder critically fails (natural 1), the bow locks up and requires a full action to unjam.

Bouncy Bonk! – The mace’s shock-absorber kicks in, halving the damage but launching the target 10 feet backwards.

Vibrating Smash! – The mace begins vibrating uncontrollably, ignoring resistance to bludgeoning damage but also making it hard to let go (DC 14 Strength save or the mace stays attached to the target until the end of your next turn).

description.p: Special Move: The "Grand Slam" (Once per Short Rest). At the end of this move, the wielder must make a DC 15 Dexterity save or be launched 10 feet backwards.

ul.li: "The Settings Wheel is Stuck": You cannot manually choose an attack mode. The settings change randomly every swing.
"Why Is It So Heavy?!": Holding the mace reduces movement speed by 5 feet.
"Sometimes It Just… Keeps Going.": If the wielder rolls a natural 1, the mace activates Flail Mode uncontrollably for 1d4 rounds (hitting the wielder and anyone nearby every turn until stopped).

"That Button Looks Suspicious": If anyone (enemy or ally) uses an action to press the red button without knowing what it does, the mace immediately activates Grand Slam Mode, whether the wielder wants it or not.

description.p: This cloak is made of dark, shimmering fabric that seems to shift and change color as it moves, resembling a night sky filled with swirling constellations. Woven into the fabric are tiny, enchanted gemstones that pulse with arcane energy.

Arcane Siphon. While wearing this cloak, you can use an action to attempt to steal a spell slot from a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The creature must have spell slots to steal. Choose a spell slot level (up to 5th level), then make a number of DC 10 + the level of the spell slot Arcana checks equal to the chosen spell slot's level. For example, if you choose a 3rd-level spell slot, you must succeed on three DC 13 Arcana checks.

description.p: These gloves are crafted from dark, supple leather with colorful, chaotic stitching that seems to shift and change as you look at it. The fingertips have embedded crystalline shards that pulse with elemental energy. When activated, these gloves unleash a burst of chaotic energy that can vary wildly in its effect, making them as dangerous to use as they are powerful.

The gloves allow the wearer to cast a variant of hellish rebuke as a reaction when they take damage. However, the effect unleashed is unpredictable and can result in both beneficial and detrimental outcomes. Using this ability also has a recoil effect on the wearer.

Chaotic Rebuke. When you take damage from a creature within 60 feet of you that you can see, you can use your reaction to point a finger at the creature and unleash a Chaotic Rebuke. Roll a d10 to determine the effect. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier), taking 3d10 damage (or another effect) on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.
Recoil. When you use the gloves, you must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or take 1d8 force damage and be pushed back 5 feet. On a success, you take no damage and are not pushed.

Runes of fate and fortune run along the handle, glowing faintly whenever the axe is swung. A thin golden chain dangles from the end of the handle, ending in a small, weighted die. This weapon draws upon the whims of luck and chaos, rewarding bold users—or punishing them for their hubris.

Fortune's Strike. When you hit a creature with this axe, you can choose to roll on the Fortune's Favor table instead of dealing normal damage. Roll a d8 to determine the effect. If you roll a 1, 2, 3, or 4, an unfavorable effect occurs; if you roll a 5, 6, 7, or 8, a favorable effect occurs.

Chaotic Edge: The target takes an additional 2d6 damage of a random element (fire, cold, lightning, or radiant). Roll a d4 to determine the type.
Fortune’s Favor: Your attack is a critical hit, regardless of the roll. Roll an additional weapon damage die.

description.p: "The Axe of Chaotic Fortune draws from the very essence of luck itself, turning each strike into a roll of fate’s dice. A swing could bring fortune or folly—only those who trust in luck dare wield it."

description.p: These stylish boots are made from supple leather and adorned with small silver buckles and embroidered with arcane runes that seem to shift in place like rolling dice. The soles are inscribed with arcane symbols that glow faintly when activated. Wearing these boots makes you feel light on your feet, but you never quite know where they’ll take you—or what will happen when they do.
Gambler’s Step. As a bonus action, you can activate the magic in these boots to attempt a teleportation effect. Roll a d6 to determine the outcome:

tr.td: d6
Result
Fumble Step: You stumble awkwardly. You teleport 5 feet in a random direction (determined by rolling a d8), and you are knocked prone.
Short Hop: You teleport 10 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, but you take 1d6 force damage from the unstable magic.
Chaotic Shift: You teleport 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, but you are disoriented, and your speed is reduced by half until the end of your next turn.
Misty Step: You cast misty step and teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
Lucky Leap: You teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, and you gain advantage on your next attack roll or ability check before the end of your next turn.

Fortune's Favor: You teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Additionally, you are surrounded by an aura of good fortune, granting you resistance to all damage until the start of your next turn.

description.p: Unpredictable Magic. After using Gambler’s Step, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest. However, if you roll a 1 on the d6, the boots lose their magical properties for 24 hours.

"The Boots of the Gambler offer a thrilling dance with fate. Every step could take you where you need to be—or somewhere entirely unexpected. Only those with luck in their veins dare to tread in these boots."
